nativeAssessment.terms: Active NASA images/media terms retained; no CC BY assertion.
nativeAssessment.dateLimits: NASA overview dates discovery to July 1989; acquisition date/UTC is not established by that discovery date. Exact acquisition and raw product crosswalk remain open. nativeAssessment.instrument: PIA02200 caption and metadata identify Voyager 2 narrow-angle camera and 155-second exposure. Filter remains unverified.
nativeAssessment.inspection: Both JPEGs show annotated 1989N4 detection amid Neptune glare/noise, faint ring arc and two star streaks. No resolved surface geography or calibrated visible colour. No new angular/raster scale calculation. TIFF retained unchanged.
nativeAssessment.processing: Publisher JPEGs and TIFF downloaded unchanged. Overview 768x788 image and PIA02200 373x438 image are distinct renditions; no byte/pixel identity or full original science-pixel preservation claim.
nativeAssessment.captionEstimates: Historical ring lengths and orbital distances are source-caption estimates, not current ephemerides, new raster measurements or uncertainties.

identityAndMetadataConflicts: NASA overview lead says Voyager 1 science team; its Discovery section says Voyager 2. PIA02200 spacecraft metadata/caption also says Voyager 2. Preserve inconsistency; do not adopt Voyager 1 as Galatea observation spacecraft.
PIA02200 image alt text describes a Galileo Jupiter hotspot, inconsistent with title, image and caption. It must not establish Jupiter provenance or geography for Galatea.
1989N4 label matches NASA overview initial designation S/1989 N4; ring arc/glare/stars are context, not Galatea terrain.
limitations: No map/globe/shape adopted or generated; no other body skin assigned.
Streaked detection is not a measured elongated shape; blur/noise does not establish local relief or material fractions.
Background blackness does not measure atmospheric absence; visible glare is not a calibrated atmosphere.
Ring-debris/collision interpretations in historical caption are hypotheses, not detected composition or direct formation history.
Exact raw product, acquisition UTC, filter, processing lineage, frame, coverage, current rotation/shape, photometry and body-specific 2026 spectroscopy audit remain open.
